thread:
ali: quick heads-up — I'm starting an adaptive-agg-window rollout for metering tonight. goal: reduce invoice spikes for bursty tenants without losing visibility. :eyes:

marta: nice. what's the plan for the console preview? we had weird negative-preview artifacts last time when windows shrank too aggressively.

ali: good call. plan is: feature-flaged rollout, start with 5% tenants, observability hooks to compare old hourly vs new adaptive per-tenant. preview will show both numbers side-by-side for 24h.

kevin: can you paste the config? curious about the heuristics.

ali: sure — current canary config:```yaml
metering.agg.window: adaptive
metering.agg.base: 5m
metering.agg.max: 1h
metering.agg.trigger: p95_latency or token_rate>500/s
metering.agg.cooldown: 10m
```

jon: so it's adaptive based on token_rate and latency p95. how do we handle tenant-level quotas/hedging? we don't want to accidentally short-window a dedicated tenant and undercount their reserved capacity.

ali: dedicated tenants are pinned to `agg.max` — feature flag will respect tenant tier. default adaptive only applies to hosted/free tiers.

marta: telemetry question: how will alerts behave? last time dashboards aggregated by the old hourly boundary and the new adaptive windows created mismatched series, breaking smoothing alerts.

ali: we're emitting a `agg_policy` tag on every metering event (`hourly|adaptive|pinned`) and adding a migration label `agg_id` so the dashboard can join by agg_id instead of timestamp bucket. that should soften the drift.

elaine: i worry about downstream invoice pipelines that assume fixed windows for compact-agg dedupe. did we update the finalizer?

kevin: @elaine good point. the compact-agg finalizer currently relies on deterministic window boundaries. adaptive introduces non-aligned windows so dedupe keys need to include `agg_id`. we prototyped this in staging and saw a 0.2% delta on invoices for sample traffic.

oncall: please add a runbook note — if we see a sudden invoice spike escalate to #oncall immediately. last rollout took us ~45m to rollback because the preview flagged but automations didn't.

ali: added runbook entry and a short circuit in the pipeline: if daily invoice delta for a tenant > 5% vs baseline AND agg_policy switched in last 24h, auto-fall back that tenant to `hourly` and create a ticket.

marta: console UX — can we make the preview toggle default to `both` for 2 weeks post-rollout? That helps product and support triage.

ali: yes, toggled. also instrumenting a lightweight evaluation: we'll compute `preview_score` = relative delta normalized by usage; flag tenants with >2% consistent drift for manual review.

jon: any API changes? we'll need client libraries to send `X-Redwood-Route-Policy` eventually for routing-aware billing, right?

ali: no API change for initial rollout. clients stay the same. we only use server-side routing heuristics. but plan is to add optional header to opt-in for experimental tenants in the future.

kevin: logging snippet from staging where agg switched:```
INFO metering: tenant=acme agg_policy=adaptive agg_id=agg-2026-06-01T03:12:45 tokens=12345 window=5m
TRACE finalizer: dedupe_key=tenant:acme:agg-2026-06-01T03:12:45
```

marta: looks good. small ask — add a per-tenant toggle in the console (opt-out) for two weeks post rollout. support will ask.

ali: done. will deploy canary at 02:00 UTC, 5% hosted tenants. i'll post a deploy-bot message when it starts. feedback welcome.

metering-bot: deploy triggered by ali — canary: adaptive-agg-window v2 -> cluster-metering-canary (5% tenants). status: queued.

oncall: tagging @oncall for night shift. if anything odd ping twice. :coffee:

elaine: thanks — i'll check the invoice preview pipeline and run a backfill compare overnight.

jon: and I'll keep an eye on quota/hedging dashboards. good luck!
